job.title: BIM / Archicad Trainer
job.description:
Design & Build are partnering with a leading Australian residential building organisation to recruit a BIM / Archicad Trainer to join their People Development function.

Based in the Hunter Region, this role will support drafting teams nationally and will involve regular travel, both interstate and nationally.

Importantly, you don't need to already be an experienced trainer.

We're equally interested in hearing from experienced Archicad 29 users, Senior Drafters, BIM specialists or technical drafting professionals who enjoy helping others and would like to pivot their career into training and development.

For the right technical person, the business is prepared to invest in your development and support you in completing your Certificate IV in Training & Assessment.

The Role
Working closely with the BIM Manager and Learning & Development team, you'll become a key technical resource supporting drafting teams across the organisation.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Delivering Archicad and BIM training to drafting teams across Australia
  • Supporting the onboarding and technical induction of new starters
  • Developing structured Archicad training programs
  • Creating training materials including guides, videos, e-learning content, job aids and SOPs
  • Running face-to-face and virtual training sessions
  • Working one-on-one and with small groups to improve technical capability
  • Identifying knowledge gaps and opportunities to improve BIM processes and training
  • Working with internal technical specialists and external BIM providers
  • Monitoring training participation and effectiveness
  • Travelling nationally to support teams across different locations
About You
There are two backgrounds we're particularly interested in:

Experienced Trainer: You may already be delivering BIM, Archicad, CAD or technical training and be looking for an opportunity within a large national organisation.

Experienced Archicad User Ready for a Career Pivot: You may be a Senior Drafter, BIM Coordinator, Archicad specialist or highly experienced residential drafting professional who loves helping others and wants to move away from day-to-day drafting into a training-focused career.
Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Strong Archicad experience – Archicad 29 highly regarded
  • A background in drafting, BIM or residential construction
  • Confidence communicating technical information in a simple way
  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills
  • An interest in coaching, mentoring and developing others
  • The ability and willingness to travel nationally
  • A proactive approach to technology and continuous improvement
  • A current driver's licence
A Certificate IV in Training & Assessment is advantageous but not essential – support can be provided to obtain this qualification for the right candidate.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is a unique opportunity to take your technical Archicad knowledge and turn it into a long-term career in training and capability development.
You'll join a major Australian building organisation, work closely with BIM and L&D specialists, gain exposure to drafting teams nationally and have the opportunity to become a recognised technical training specialist within the business.
If you're an Archicad expert who's always the person others come to for help, this could be the career pivot you've been looking for.

Apply now or contact Renee Hamilton at Design & Build Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Information Access Manager
job.description:
Location: Sydney, NSW
Salary: $178,021 to $203,376 + 12% Super
Work Type: Full Time, Permanent
Public Sector People on behalf of City of Sydney

Lead the City's information access function and become the trusted expert driving transparency, sound decision making and best practice governance across one of Australia's most progressive councils.

Public Sector People are proud to partner with the City of Sydney to recruit an Information Access Manager within the Digital and Information Services Unit.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced GIPA or Freedom of Information professional to lead the City's information access function as its delegated decision-maker under the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009. Leading a specialist team, you'll make complex statutory decisions, provide trusted advice to the Executive Leadership Team and work across every area of the organisation to ensure the City continues to uphold the principles of transparency, accountability and open government.

This is a role for someone who enjoys applying legislation to complex situations, can confidently make independent decisions and has the judgement to navigate sensitive matters with professionalism, diplomacy and integrity.

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Information Services, you will be responsible for:
  • Lead and develop the City's specialist Information Access team.
  • Act as the City's delegated decision-maker under the GIPA Act.
  • Assess and determine complex GIPA applications, subpoenas and other information access matters.
  • Provide expert advice to Directors, Executives and business units on information access legislation and disclosure obligations.
  • Represent the City in reviews with the Information and Privacy Commission and NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT).
  • Drive proactive release initiatives and promote a culture of open government across the organisation.
  • Develop policies, procedures and education programs that strengthen legislative compliance and organisational capability.
  • Work collaboratively with Legal, Governance, Archives and operational teams to resolve complex information access matters.
 
 
What You'll Bring
  • Extensive experience administering the Government Information (Public Access) Act (GIPA) or equivalent Freedom of Information legislation.
  • Demonstrated experience making independent statutory decisions within a complex public sector environment.
  • Strong understanding of balancing transparency with public interest considerations and legislative obligations.
  • Experience advising senior executives and confidently influencing stakeholders on sensitive matters.
  • Leadership experience managing and developing high-performing specialist teams.
  • Excellent judgement, resilience and communication skills, with the confidence to make, explain and defend complex decisions.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Information Management, Governance or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.


Why City of Sydney?
  • Lead the City's information access function as the delegated decision-maker under the GIPA Act.
  • Make decisions that directly influence transparency, governance and public trust.
  • Work closely with senior executives, Legal and Governance on complex and high-profile matters.
  • Join one of Australia's leading local government organisations, committed to innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  
Ready to become the trusted authority on information access at the City of Sydney?

Contact Esme Lynch at Public Sector People on 0413 282 765 or email esme@publicsectorpeople.com.au for a confidential discussion.

Applications close: 11:59pm, Thursday 15th October 2026.

Essential:

job.title: Project Manager (Housing)
job.description:
Project Manager (Housing)
 
A new building is only part of the picture. Making it ready for people to call home takes coordinated planning, clear decisions and strong operational leadership.
 
Public Sector People is seeking a Project Manager for a purpose-led organisation delivering social and affordable housing across Greater Brisbane and surrounding areas.
 
This role will bring new housing developments, acquisitions and service expansions into operation, ensuring properties, teams, systems and services are ready before residents move in.
 
Based in Brisbane, with travel to development and property sites, you will lead a team of two and work across the organisation to coordinate delivery, resolve challenges and oversee the transition into stable day-to-day operations.
 
The opportunity
 
You will take ownership of the operational readiness program, translating development commitments into practical plans with clear milestones, responsibilities and measures of success.
 
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading readiness plans across multiple projects, managing timelines, budgets, resources, risks and dependencies.
  • Coordinating property handovers, including asset information, defects, compliance documentation, utilities and contractor mobilisation.
  • Bringing together tenant allocations, sign-ups, move-ins and customer communications to support a coordinated occupancy process.
  • Ensuring systems, data, procedures, staffing and training are prepared and tested before opening.
  • Leading cross-functional working groups and working with developers, builders, government agencies, contractors and service partners.
  • Providing executive reporting and recommendations on readiness, emerging risks and decisions required.
  • Supporting early operations and transferring outstanding actions and ongoing responsibilities to the relevant teams.
About you
 
You will bring substantial experience delivering complex projects, operational mobilisation, service transitions or major change initiatives involving multiple teams and stakeholders.
 
You can turn competing requirements into a clear delivery plan, build commitment across business functions and make sound decisions when priorities shift.
 
You will also bring:
  • Strong project governance skills, including integrated planning, risk management, assurance and executive reporting.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing stakeholders across an organisation.
  • Financial and commercial capability, including budget management, forecasting, procurement and supplier coordination.
  • Clear communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
  • Practical knowledge of WHS, privacy, records management and operational compliance.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification or an equivalent combination of expertise and senior project experience.
  • A current Queensland driver licence and willingness to complete a National Police Check.
Experience in community housing, human services, property development, construction handover or asset management would be valuable. Experience opening new residential properties or services, implementing systems or managing data migration would also be well regarded.
 
What's on offer
  • Full-time hours, 38 hours per week.
  • A broad leadership role with autonomy and visibility across the organisation.
  • The opportunity to shape how new housing and services are brought into operation.
  • Work that contributes to safe, secure and affordable homes.
To apply
 
Apply with your resume outlining your relevant project delivery and operational mobilisation experience.

For a confidential discussion, contact Ebonnie Goss at Public Sector People.

  • Identify and resolve requirement gaps, conflicts, dependencies and risks, ensuring requirements remain traceable throughout design, testing and implementation.
  • Facilitate workshops with business, technical and vendor stakeholders to gather requirements, solve issues and support delivery, testing and operational readiness.
  

The ideal candidate will have:

  • Experience working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, driving analysis activities and achieving stakeholder alignment across business, technical and vendor teams.
  
Highly Desirable attributes:
  • Experience in regulated or operational environments such as government, transport, compliance, enforcement or safety-critical industries.
  • Background working with asset management or enterprise asset management platforms, ideally Hardcat or similar COTS solutions.
  • Experience with APIs, system integrations, data synchronisation and integration monitoring.
  • Strong data migration experience involving complex legacy system transitions.
  • Experience working with software vendors, implementation partners and managed service providers.

job.title: Coordinator Open Spaces Strategy
job.description:
Clarence Valley Council is seeking an experienced and versatile leader to coordinate the strategic planning, asset management and capital delivery of its extensive open-space network.
  
Covering an area of more than 10,000 square kilometres and incorporating communities including Grafton, Maclean and Yamba, the Clarence Valley offers the opportunity to work across a varied portfolio of parks, reserves, sporting facilities, beaches, aquatic facilities and public recreation infrastructure.
  
The Role
Reporting to the Manager Open Spaces and Facilities, you will lead Council’s Open Spaces Strategy team and coordinate the long-term planning and improvement of the open-space network.
  
This is a broad, strategic position rather than an operational parks role. You will connect planning, asset management and project delivery to ensure Council makes informed, sustainable decisions about its public spaces and facilities.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading the development and review of open-space strategies, policies, masterplans and providing advice to inform the development of plans of management
  • Improving asset management plans, service levels and lifecycle planning across the open-space portfolio
  • Coordinating the planning, procurement and delivery of capital works projects
  • Managing service contracts and licence agreements relating to aquatic, sporting and beach facilities
  • Providing professional advice on development applications and projects affecting public open space, landscaping, vegetation and trees
  • Responding to emerging asset issues and balancing reactive requests with longer-term priorities
  • Preparing Council reports, funding applications, project documentation and evidence-based recommendations
  • Leading a multidisciplinary team and working closely with operational staff, contractors, community groups and internal stakeholders
About You
You will be an established leader who can operate across several disciplines rather than working within one narrow area of expertise.

You may come from open-space planning, asset management, engineering, landscape architecture, recreation planning, urban and regional planning or capital project delivery. More important than a particular professional background is your ability to connect strategic planning with practical implementation.

You will bring:
  • Experience developing strategies, policies, masterplans or asset management plans
  • Practical experience delivering capital works or construction-related projects
  • Sound project, contract and budget management capability
  • Established leadership experience and the ability to provide clear direction to a multidisciplinary team
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • The judgement to manage competing priorities and politically or publicly sensitive matters
  • The ability to interpret asset data, technical information, planning requirements and Council policies
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or an equivalent combination of qualifications and experience
Local government experience will be highly regarded, particularly where you have worked across community-facing services and managed changing operational and political priorities.

The Opportunity
This position offers a rare opportunity to influence the future of a diverse and highly visible community asset portfolio. You will have the scope to strengthen Council’s strategic and asset management approach while delivering projects that directly shape how residents and visitors experience the Clarence Valley.
  
Council offers:
  • A permanent full-time position
  • Salary of $108,853–$129,809 plus superannuation
  • 70 hours per fortnight
  • Flexible working hours and access to flex time
  • Five days of MyLeave each year, which can be used flexibly for any purpose
  • Professional development and career progression opportunities
  • The lifestyle benefits of living and working in the NSW Northern Rivers
Applications close Tuesday 20th October 2026, 11:30 pm.

Will Cooke
Senior Consultant – Public Sector People

wcooke@publicsectorpeople.com.au

The Successful Candidate

  • At least three years’ experience in a town planning or strategic planning role, particularly involving the development of strategic planning instruments.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce high-quality reports and advice.

Desirable experience includes:

job.title: Planning Coordinator
job.description:
About Strathbogie Shire Council

Strathbogie Shire Council is a progressive regional municipality encompassing communities including Euroa, Nagambie, Avenel and Violet Town, ideally positioned between Melbourne and Shepparton.

Council is committed to delivering responsive, consistent and customer-focused planning services while supporting the sustainable growth and development of the Shire.

With a capable team in place and several significant planning matters progressing across the municipality, this is an opportunity to provide experienced leadership, strengthen internal capability and help shape the continued development of Council’s planning function.

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Planning and Investment, the Planning Coordinator will lead Council’s statutory planning function while contributing to strategic planning projects, planning scheme amendments and broader service improvement initiatives.

This is a hands-on leadership position. You will provide clear direction and technical guidance to a developing team while personally managing complex and sensitive planning applications, including major subdivisions and proposals attracting significant community or Councillor interest.

You will oversee workloads, priorities and service standards, review technical assessments and reports, and support planners to develop their judgement, confidence and understanding of the Victorian planning system.

The role will work closely with applicants, internal stakeholders, referral authorities, community members and Councillors. You will prepare and present reports directly to Council, brief Councillors on significant planning matters and represent Council at VCAT, panel hearings and other planning forums when required.

While the role is weighted toward statutory planning, exposure to strategic planning will be highly regarded. You will also support policy development, planning scheme amendments and longer-term growth initiatives, enabling the Manager to focus more broadly across the performance and strategic direction of the unit.

About You

You are an experienced statutory and strategic planning professional ready to take genuine ownership of a small and important planning function.
You bring strong technical knowledge of the Planning and Environment Act, the Victorian Planning Provisions and contemporary local government planning practice. You are confident assessing complex applications, preparing defensible recommendations and navigating matters involving competing stakeholder, community and political interests.

Just as importantly, you are a capable people leader. You can set expectations, manage performance and workloads, develop emerging planners and create a culture of accountability, collaboration and support. You enjoy sharing your knowledge but also understand that leadership is about enabling others to perform rather than simply providing technical answers.

You are comfortable operating with autonomy and do not require significant day-to-day direction. You can identify issues early, exercise sound professional judgement and provide your Manager with the confidence that the statutory planning function is being effectively led.

Customer service is central to your approach. You communicate clearly, manage difficult conversations constructively and understand the importance of helping applicants and community members.

Most importantly, you are motivated by the opportunity to lead, support a developing team and build a high-performing planning service within a growing regional municipality.

Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Strathbogie Shire Council to recruit this important leadership opportunity.

For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the Position Description, please contact Marcel Lafontaine at Public Sector People -
marcel@publicsectorpeople.com.au.

job.title: State Manager
job.description:
Design & Build is looking for a proven recruitment leader to take ownership of our WA business and lead its next stage of growth.

This is not a turnaround role.

You will inherit a healthy six-person team, an established client base, a recognised national brand and a Perth business that has grown year on year since launching in 2021.

The opportunity is to build on that foundation and establish one of WA’s leading specialist recruitment businesses.

The opportunity

This is a billing State Manager position, combining leadership of the WA team with continued ownership of a specialist recruitment market.

Energy & Resources is a significant growth opportunity for the business, but we are open to shaping the desk around the experience, relationships and market knowledge of the right person.

You will lead from the front by developing clients, building your market, billing personally and helping the team perform and grow. Once the WA business reaches 12 people, your personal billing responsibilities will transition out, allowing you to focus fully on leadership, strategy and continued expansion.

You will report directly to Andrew McGregor, Managing Director, with the autonomy and support to shape the future of the WA business.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing the existing WA team
  • Building a high-performing specialist recruitment market
  • Growing relationships with clients across WA
  • Attracting experienced recruiters into the business
  • Setting clear standards around activity, performance and accountability
  • Identifying new markets and growth opportunities
  • Protecting and strengthening the culture as the team scales
  • Taking ownership of the WA strategy and P&L
Who we are looking for

Energy & Resources recruitment experience would be highly regarded, but it is not essential.

More important is a strong understanding of the WA market, a proven ability to build lasting client relationships and established credibility within a specialist recruitment sector.

We are open to leaders from Energy, Resources, Construction, Engineering, Infrastructure, Property or other related technical markets.

You may already be operating at State Manager level, or you may be a successful Team Leader or Manager who is ready to take the next step.

You will bring:
  • A strong background in specialist recruitment within the WA market
  • At least one to two years’ experience leading a small team
  • A proven personal billing track record
  • The ability to win work and build lasting client relationships
  • A genuine interest in developing people and growing a business
  • A leadership style aligned with our values of Honest Communication, Focus, Feedback and Care
Why Design & Build?

Design & Build has been operating for more than 20 years, with offices in Perth, Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.

Our vision is to become Australia’s most trusted recruitment agency. We measure ourselves against a simple mission: doing right by our clients, candidates, colleagues and community.

You will also receive:
  • A 35-hour working week with flexibility around start and finish times
  • Two work-from-home days each week
  • A fully paid Christmas shutdown in addition to annual leave
  • An additional day of leave for every year of service, providing up to 30 days of annual leave after five years
  • An annual all-expenses-paid High Achievers trip
  • Structured leadership development and ongoing coaching
  • Free and unlimited access to Sonder’s 24/7 wellbeing and safety support
  • Enhanced parental and compassionate leave
  • Support from experienced national leaders across operations, finance, people and culture, learning and development, and marketing
This is a genuine opportunity to inherit a strong platform, lead an established team and build a substantial WA recruitment business.

If you are an experienced recruitment leader ready to take ownership of a state and shape its next stage of growth, we would like to hear from you.

Apply confidentially or contact Andrew McGregor for a direct conversation.

job.title: Procurement Specialist
job.description:
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Procurement / Commercial professional to support with the procurement of major projects up to $1b.

You will work closely with construction, estimating, and commercial teams to ensure trade packages are competitively procured, commercially sound, and aligned with program and delivery objectives.


Key Responsibilities
  • Manage hands-on procurement across up to 20 trade packages
  • Issue tender packages to market and coordinate supplier engagement
  • Liaise with construction and delivery teams to arrange supplier meetings and clarifications
  • Conduct commercial analysis including cost comparisons, valuations, and bid assessments
  • Review and interpret conditions of offer, inclusions/exclusions, and scope alignment
  • Support bid strategy development including options analysis and risk evaluation
  • Assess productivity impacts and program implications of subcontractor selections
  • Track and manage tender schedules, submissions, and procurement timelines
  • Deliver cost analysis and benchmarking to ensure best value outcomes
  • Contribute to end-to-end bid submissions (targeted for end of July)
  • Maintain strong awareness of market conditions and local trade capabilities
  • Ensure alignment with project sensitivities, including preference for local subcontractors where required
  • Support external valuation and commercial reporting requirements

Key Projects
  • Packages include numerous major projects including Defence, Sport Stadiums, Infrastructure, on JV delivery models

Working Environment
  • Based in a Melbourne CBD bidding office
  • Fast-paced tender environment with multiple concurrent bids

About You
  • Strong background in construction procurement or commercial management
  • Experience handling multiple trade packages simultaneously
  • Confident in cost analysis, commercial evaluation, and bid preparation
  • Strong numerical and analytical capability
  • Understanding of construction programs, productivity, and sequencing impacts
  • Ability to manage complex supplier and subcontractor negotiations
  • Strong market awareness and supplier network knowledge
  • Comfortable working in a high-pressure, deadline-driven bidding environment

Process
  • Initial contract engagement with potential for a permanent role
  • Interview process led in person at the Melbourne CBD office
  • Quick turnaround recruitment process

job.description:
Public Sector People are partnering with the QLD State Government Department who are seeking an experienced Health and Wellbeing Principal Advisor (AO7) to lead and continuously improve enterprise-wide programs that protect worker health and support a safe, healthy and productive workforce.
  
Overview:
  • ASAP Start | Health and Wellbeing Principal Advisor (A07)
  • Attractive hourly rate from $87 per hour + 12% super
  • Initial contract until 31st March 2027 with potential for extension
  • QLD State Government
  • Brisbane CBD
  
Summary:

This specialist role leads worker health, wellbeing, fitness for work and hazardous exposure initiatives across a large Queensland civil construction workforce. Leveraging technical expertise, stakeholder engagement and organisational influence, the position drives enterprise-wide health outcomes, solves complex workforce challenges and delivers practical business-wide solutions without direct people management responsibilities.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead worker health programs including health monitoring, surveillance, contractor management and governance to ensure compliance and effective workforce health outcomes.
  • Oversee fitness for work and wellbeing initiatives, covering fatigue management, drug and alcohol programs, psychosocial risk management and employee wellbeing.

  • Provide specialist advice and drive continuous improvement by developing policies, standards and practical organisation-wide solutions to health and wellbeing challenges.
What we are looking for:

The successful candidate will have access to occupational hygiene and specialist technical support when required; however, they will be expected to provide leadership, governance and program management across these disciplines and help continue maturing its approach to worker health and wellbeing.
  • Available ASAP, more than five years' experience in health, occupational hygiene, workplace wellbeing, health and safety or a closely related field.
  • Experience within construction, civil construction, transport, infrastructure, utilities, resources, rail or other comparable high-risk industries.
  • Strong experience implementing and managing fit-for-work programs, including fatigue and drug and alcohol management, leading psychosocial risk management programs and workplace wellbeing initiatives.
  • Experience developing enterprise-level frameworks, systems, standards, procedures and improvement programs, managing health risks associated with hazardous substances and hazardous exposures.

**This is a highly competitive role, and the hiring manager will be moving fast**
  
As an approved Government recruitment partner Public Sector People are ideally placed to assist you in your search for your next temporary or permanent opportunity.   
   
Best of luck!
